heading: Security
body:
Every response carries defensive security headers. One of them is a strict content security policy. This header tells the browser which content the page may load. The policy is `script-src 'self'`, no inline script, `object-src 'none'` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`. There are two inline scripts. The speculation rules block lets the browser fetch a linked page before the click. A one-line view transition guard keeps the browser quiet when a fast click skips the animation between two pages; without it, Chromium reports `AbortError: Transition was skipped`. The policy allows both by the SHA-256 hash of their text, which every browser understands. Chrome's own keyword for it, `'inline-speculation-rules'`, made Safari warn on every page and refuse the block. Every native host (macOS, iOS, Android, Windows and Linux) sends a policy built from the same source, so its web view allows the same scripts, the hashes included. A native policy also allows images and fonts over `https:`, lets a page frame documents from its own bundle as the web does, and its `connect-src` allows the app's own bundle and the hosts in `tac.outgoing.hosts` only. The Android host writes its bridge script into each page, so its policy also allows that one script by its hash. A controller call runs as one process with limits: a deadline and a concurrency limit (the most requests it runs at the same time). Its protocol frames (the messages it exchanges with the server) are limited to 16 MiB. The server checks each argument against the types of the controller method. This happens before Tachyon calls the method.

Every route says who may call it (`Public`, `SignedIn` or `Allow(Role)`), and one `IdentityProvider` class says who is signed in. The server answers 401 or 403 before the method runs (see Who may call a route). How users sign in stays with the application: the identity provider reads a session or a token in the language's own request type. Tachyon has no CORS (cross-origin resource sharing) layer; a middleware runs its `before` method before every request, and that policy goes there. The policy's `connect-src` allows the page's own origin and the hosts in `tac.outgoing.hosts` only.
